statement.p: Calculate the following integral: \int x \sec^{2}\mathopen{}\left(-8x\right) \, dx
and then use the integration-by-parts formula to find that
and finally, we finish evaluating to get that \displaystyle \int \sec^{2}\mathopen{}\left(-8x\right) x \, dx =

hint.p: We pick u and dv so that dv can be integrated, and then (ideally) u gets simpler.
Both x and \sec^{2}\mathopen{}\left(-8x\right) can be easily integrated, so pick them so that u gets simpler.
Then dv =\sec^{2}\mathopen{}\left(-8x\right)dx, and we integrate to get that v= \frac{1}{-8} \tan(-8 x)
Remember that even though it's not Basic, you do know how to integrate \tan(-8 x). It's number 7 on the u-Substitution practice worksheet we did in class.

solution.p: The integration by parts formula says that \int u \, dv = u\cdot v - \int v \, du So, substituting in, we get that \int x \sec^{2}\mathopen{}\left(-8x\right) \, dx = x \cdot \frac{1}{-8} \tan(-8 x) - \int \frac{1}{-8} \tan(-8 x) \, dx =\frac{1}{-8} x \tan(-8 x) - \int \frac{1}{-8} \tan(-8 x) \, dx Unfortunately, the integral is not Basic, but we can rewrite it and integrate it using u-substitution. \frac{1}{-8} x \tan(-8 x) - \int \frac{1}{-8} \frac{\sin(-8 x)}{\cos(-8 x)} \, dx Let u=\cos(-8 x) so du = + 8 \sin(-8 x) \, dx and solving for dx gives us dx=\frac{du}{ + 8 \sin(-8 x)}.

Substituting back into the integral gives us: \int \frac{1}{-8} \frac{\sin(-8 x)}{\cos(-8 x)} \, dx = \int \frac{1}{-8} \frac{\sin(-8 x)}{u} \, \frac{du}{ + 8 \sin(-8 x)} = \int \frac{-1}{64} \frac{du}{u} This integrates to \frac{-1}{64} \ln(u) and substituting back in for u gives \frac{-1}{64} \ln(\cos(-8 x))+C Combining it with the non-integrated term from integration by parts, we get the final answer: \int x \sec^{2}\mathopen{}\left(-8x\right) \, dx = \frac{1}{-8} x \tan(-8 x) - \frac{-1}{64} \ln(\cos(-8 x))+C
